newsitem.title: MEXICO: Enserch Corp, Mexico firm eye natgas plans.
newsitem.headline: Enserch Corp, Mexico firm eye natgas plans.

text.p: Enserch Corp. and Mexican partner Compania Mexicana de Gas, plan to invest $50 million through the year 2005 on natural gas distribution projects, company officials said on Wednesday.

The Mexican firm's board chairman Luis Vazquez talked about investment plans here when signing its partnership with Enserch. The Dallas, Texas-based company recently bought a 49 percent stake in Compania Mexicana de Gas. "We now have $50 million invested and plan to invest another $50 million here by the year $50 million," Vazquez said.
The partnership plans to bid for natural gas distribution rights being privatized in Toluca, Tampico and Altamira and Mexico City.
Compania Mexicana de Gas already distributes natural gas in Monterrey, along with state monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) and the Federal Electricity Commission.

The company has applied to continue distributing natural gas in the region, and Monterrey director general Marcelo Chauvet said the company was given a five-year temporary permit. A Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) source said the commission had not yet decided on whether to grant the permit.
Monterrey was recently designated the latest in a series of zones where natural gas distribution rights are being sold to private companies.
Compania Mexicana de Gas is also bidding for the official longer-term permit. Bidding for the site is scheduled to be opened in the coming months.
The company has a 250 km (155 mile) distribution system in Monterrey and sells more than 65 million cubic feet per month of natural gas.
